Fit a latent transition model of how units move between latent states over repeated occasions

Source: R/transitions.R
lta.Rd

lta() fits a latent transition model, which describes stability and change in latent states across repeated occasions. The states (profiles) are patterns in continuous or discrete indicators; transition probabilities give the chance of staying in a state or moving to another between successive occasions. The measurement and transition parameters are estimated jointly.

By default the chain is first order and time-homogeneous: the state at an occasion depends on the state before it, with the same transition matrix at every occasion. The measurement parameters are shared across occasions and across group classes, so a state means the same thing throughout and group classes differ only in their initial distribution and transitions. Options add covariate-dependent transitions, occasion-specific transitions or measurement, second-order dependence, a mover-stayer class, sampling weights and ordinal or count indicators; any of these changes the result class (see Value).

Usage

lta(
  data,
  vars,
  id,
  n_profiles,
  time,
  n_group_classes = 1L,
  variance_model = c("varying", "equal"),
  n_starts = 10L,
  max_iter = 5000L,
  tol = 1e-10,
  min_variance = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  missing = c("error", "fiml"),
  covariance_model = c("diagonal", "full"),
  categorical = character(),
  min_probability = 1e-10,
  occasions = c("observed", "grid"),
  select_start = c("likelihood", "converged"),
  transitions = c("homogeneous", "occasion"),
  transition_covariates = character(),
  initial_covariates = character(),
  measurement = c("invariant", "occasion"),
  order = 1L,
  model = NULL,
  mover_stayer = FALSE,
  weights = NULL,
  ordinal = character(),
  count = character(),
  count_model = c("poisson", "negative_binomial"),
  count_dispersion = c("varying", "equal"),
  drop_empty = TRUE,
  search = c("kmeans", "emEM"),
  n_screen = NULL,
  acceleration = c("squarem", "none"),
  cores = 1L
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with the indicators and the group identifier.

vars

Names of the indicator columns. Those not named in categorical, ordinal or count are continuous.

id

Name of the column identifying the units (persons) whose occasions are followed (character, factor or numeric, without missing values). Required.

n_profiles

Number of profiles, at least two.

time

Column giving each row's occasion within its group. Required; values must be unique within a group and sort in their intended order (numbers numerically, factors by level, text alphabetically, so "T2", "T10" is refused; use a factor or zero-pad).

n_group_classes

Number of group classes (default 1). With 1, every unit follows the same initial and transition probabilities. More than one fits a mixture of transition models: each unit belongs to one group class, and each group class has its own initial and transition probabilities.

variance_model

Whether the profiles share the variances of the continuous indicators:

  • "varying" (default): each profile has its own variances (its own covariance matrix under covariance_model = "full"), so profiles can differ in spread as well as in level;

  • "equal": one set of variances (one covariance matrix) shared by all profiles, so profiles differ only in their means. This uses fewer parameters and is less prone to solutions in which one profile's variance collapses towards zero.

n_starts

Number of EM starts (default 10). The first is deterministic (Ward's clustering), the rest random; the reported start need not have converged, so check converged. See Starts and convergence under multilpa().

max_iter

Maximum EM updates per start (default 5000). The fit warns when its reported start stopped short. max_iter = 0 evaluates the starting values without updating them and reports converged = FALSE.

tol

Convergence tolerance (default 1e-10): EM stops when a step changes the log likelihood by no more than tol times the number of observed indicator values.

min_variance

Lower bound on every variance (on every covariance eigenvalue under full covariance). NULL (default) uses 1e-6 times the smallest sample variance of the continuous indicators, on the scale fitted; a number is an absolute bound in squared indicator units. An estimate at the bound is a boundary solution and warns.

seed

Optional integer seed. The caller's random-number state is restored on exit.

missing

What to do with missing indicator values:

  • "error" (default): stop, naming the indicators that have them;

  • "fiml": keep every row and fit each one on the indicators it observes (full-information maximum likelihood), valid when the missingness depends only on observed values. A row with no observed indicator keeps its place in the sequence.

Covariates must be complete either way. See Occasions without data.

covariance_model

Whether continuous indicators are correlated within a profile:

  • "diagonal" (default): no covariances, so within a profile the indicators are independent and all their association is explained by the profiles;

  • "full": the within-profile covariances are estimated, one matrix per profile under variance_model = "varying" and one shared matrix under "equal".

With variance_model this gives four of the structures of model: VVI ("varying" and "diagonal"), EEI ("equal" and "diagonal"), VVV ("varying" and "full") and EEE ("equal" and "full").

categorical

Indicators modelled by profile-specific response probabilities over their observed categories, the latent class measurement model. Binary, ordered and unordered indicators share this parameterization. Naming a subset of vars fits a mixed-mode model.

min_probability

Lower bound on every categorical response probability (default 1e-10).

occasions

How a group's rows are placed on the sequence of occasions:

  • "observed" (default): each group's own rows are numbered consecutively, so a transition always links two adjacent rows, whatever the gap between their time values;

  • "grid": the rows are placed on the grid of every time value seen in the data, so a group that skips a value still makes a transition across the gap and contributes no measurement at it.

The two agree when every group is observed at every time value. Under either, a group's first row is its first occasion: occasion-specific transitions and measurement count occasions from each group's own start, not from the first time value in the data.

select_start

Which start is reported:

  • "likelihood" (default): the start with the highest log likelihood, whether or not it converged. Among starts tied within the convergence tolerance, a converged one is preferred;

  • "converged": the start with the highest log likelihood among those that converged, or among all starts when none converged.

summary() and get_results(fit, "starts") report every start.

transitions

Whether the transition probabilities change over occasions:

  • "homogeneous" (default): one transition matrix for every move, so the chance of moving from one profile to another is the same at every occasion;

  • "occasion": a separate matrix for each move (occasion 1 to 2, 2 to 3, and so on), with n_profiles * (n_profiles - 1) more parameters per group class for each additional move.

See Occasions without data.

transition_covariates

Columns whose values shift the transition probabilities through a multinomial logit per origin profile (the log odds of moving to each other profile rather than staying). A column may change over occasions; the value at the destination occasion is used. Factors are expanded to indicator columns after dropping unused levels. With occasions = "grid", a skipped position has no row to read the covariates from and is refused: use "observed", or add the skipped rows with their covariate values and missing indicators under FIML. The default, character(), is no covariates.

initial_covariates

Columns that shift the initial profile distribution (a multinomial logit, last profile as reference), read at each group's first occasion. Factors are expanded as for transition_covariates. The default, character(), is no covariates.

measurement

Whether the profiles keep their definition over occasions:

  • "invariant" (default): the profiles' means, variances and response probabilities are equal at every occasion, so a profile means the same thing throughout and a transition is a change of profile;

  • "occasion": they are estimated separately at each occasion. The profiles may then drift, and the same label need not mean the same thing at two occasions.

order

The order of the chain:

  • 1 (default): the profile at an occasion depends on the profile at the previous occasion only;

  • 2: from the third occasion on it depends on the profiles at the two previous occasions; the first transition stays first order. This needs at least three occasions.

model

The covariance structure as one of mclust's fourteen codes ("EII", "VII", "EEI", "VEI", "EVI", "VVI", "EEE", "VEE", "EVE", "VVE", "EEV", "VEV", "EVV", "VVV"), explained under multilpa(). NULL (default) follows variance_model and covariance_model. Unlike in multilpa(), a model given together with variance_model or covariance_model is not refused: model is used and the other two are ignored. A multilpa_transitions fit gives standard errors for EEI, VVI, EEE and VVV only; a multilpa_lta fit (see Value) gives them for every structure.

mover_stayer

FALSE (default) fits the model as described. TRUE adds a class of stayers: units that never change profile, with their own initial distribution (the mover-stayer model). It separates units that are stable throughout from units that can move. n_group_classes then counts the mover classes only, and the stayer class is reported as "stayers".

weights

Name of a column holding one sampling weight per id (constant over its occasions): pseudo maximum likelihood with sandwich standard errors, as under multilpa(). The model-implied "transitions" and "initial" tables then average the units with their weights. NULL (default) weights every unit equally.

ordinal, count, count_model, count_dispersion

Ordinal and count indicators, as under multilpa(): count_model is "poisson" (default) or "negative_binomial", and count_dispersion is "varying" (default, one dispersion per profile) or "equal". With measurement = "occasion" their parameters are estimated per occasion. Read with get_results(fit, "ordinal") and get_results(fit, "count_means").

drop_empty

TRUE (default) leaves rows with no observed indicator, and groups made only of such rows, out of the sample sizes, entropies and classification tables, as Mplus does, keeping their rows with NA in the assignment tables. FALSE counts them in the entropies, the tables and the number of groups, so the criteria over groups and those using the entropy change; the number of rows in the individual-level criteria stays the informative rows for profile and class models. For transition models, FALSE also counts all positive-weight rows in the individual-level BIC. Estimation is the same either way; fits with different settings are not compared.

search

How the starting values are searched:

  • "kmeans" (default): every one of the n_starts starts is run to convergence;

  • "emEM": a larger pool of n_screen starts is screened with a short EM run each, and only the first start and the best of the rest, n_starts in all, are run to convergence.

Unlike multilpa(), lta() does not pick the default by covariance structure.

n_screen

For search = "emEM" only, the size of the screened pool (default five times n_starts, at least n_starts). It is refused under search = "kmeans", the default.

acceleration

How EM is run:

  • "squarem" (default): EM accelerated with SQUAREM, which usually needs fewer iterations and never lowers the likelihood;

  • "none": plain EM.

cores

Number of processor cores for the starts (default 1); with seed the result is identical to one core. To fit several models, give cores to enumerate_classes() instead.

Value

A fitted model of one of two classes.

multilpa_transitions is returned for the basic model: continuous or categorical indicators, homogeneous first-order transitions, invariant measurement, no covariates, no stayer class and no weights. get_results() returns its tables by name, among them:

  • "transitions": one row per group class, origin profile (from) and destination profile (to), with the transition probability, the expected number of moves, and the flags supported and estimated (see Occasions without data);

  • "initial": the probability of each profile at the first occasion and its prevalence over all occasions;

  • "profiles" (also as.data.frame(fit)) and "responses": the profile means and variances, and the response probabilities of categorical indicators;

  • "assignments": the data with each row's most likely profile, its unit's group class and the posterior probabilities;

  • "sequences", "sequence_summary" and "sequence_lengths": the profile assigned to each unit at each occasion, and the lengths of the sequences;

  • "classification", "entropy", "information_criteria" and "starts", as for a multilpa() fit.

Profiles and group classes are numbered 1, 2, and so on.

multilpa_lta is returned when any of these is used: transitions = "occasion", transition_covariates, initial_covariates, measurement = "occasion", order = 2, mover_stayer = TRUE, weights, ordinal or count. Its tables:

  • "transitions" (also as.data.frame(fit)): the model-implied transition probabilities, per occasion where they differ, with supported and estimated;

  • "transition_coefficients" and "initial_coefficients": the logit coefficients with Wald standard errors, confidence limits and odds ratios;

  • "initial": the initial profile probabilities;

  • "profiles": the measurement parameters, per occasion under measurement = "occasion";

  • "group_classes": the proportion of each group class, the stayers included;

  • "assignments", "posteriors", "entropy", "information_criteria", "fit" and "starts".

The parameter tables of this class label profiles and group classes "profile_1", "group_class_1", and so on; its "assignments" table numbers them.

For both classes parameter_inference() gives Wald or bootstrap standard errors, bootstrap_lrt() compares nested fits, plot_transitions() draws the transition probabilities and plot_sequences() the sequences. Profile labels are arbitrary and not comparable across fits without alignment.

Conditions

Errors: latents_bad_argument when id or time is left out or an argument has a value that is not accepted; latents_bad_data for a column that data does not have or missing indicator values under missing = "error"; latents_bad_time for time values that repeat within a group or do not sort; latents_bad_transition for fewer than two profiles, for data in which no group is observed at two occasions or no indicator is observed after the first occasion, and for order = 2 with fewer than three occasions; latents_unidentified for the specifications listed under Short panels and bootstrap support, and for more profiles than distinct rows or more group classes than groups; latents_bad_covariate for a constant or collinear covariate.

Warnings: latents_unconverged when the reported start stopped at max_iter; latents_boundary when a variance or a probability is at its bound; latents_empty_transition_row, latents_weak_transition_support and latents_unidentified_occasion for the cases under Occasions without data; latents_small_classes when a profile or group class has an effective size below one; latents_failed_starts when some starts failed. latents-conditions lists every condition.

Occasions without data

A transition the data never observe is not estimated. A profile that no unit of a group class occupies before the unit's last occasion has no move out of it: its row of the transition matrix is uniform by construction, flagged estimated = FALSE, not counted in n_parameters, AIC or BIC, and reported with a warning. On a multilpa_transitions fit, get_results(fit, "transitions", estimated = FALSE) lists such rows. Nonzero origins with fewer than one expected outgoing move trigger a weak- support warning. Transition tables show origin_expected_count and supported; Wald inference is withheld. These nonzero rows remain formally estimated and counted in the criteria: this is a support diagnostic, not a declaration of structural non-identification. Homogeneous rows pool support across their applicable moves; occasion- specific rows use that occasion's count. The averaged second-order table reports the total count, but supported is false if any separately fitted occasion has fewer than one expected outgoing move.

Under FIML, three more things are unidentified and flagged the same way: under transitions = "occasion", a move into an occasion at which no row observes an indicator (after the last observed occasion it does not enter the likelihood; before it, only through its product with the move out); under order = 2, the second-order logits when nothing is observed from occasion 3 on; under measurement = "occasion", the measurement block of an empty occasion.

For second-order occasion-specific chains, an empty interior occasion does not use the first-order product rule: remaining logits stay counted and the parameter count is an upper bound. A second-order fit's first-order table describes only the move into occasion 2. The second-order table averages over groups and applicable occasions, with move-frequency weights.

Short panels and bootstrap support

Without initial or transition covariates, two occasions cannot identify multiple group classes or a separate stayer class. Three occasions cannot identify multiple freely moving group classes with occasion-specific transitions, or multiple classes in a second-order chain. These specifications are refused; convergence cannot resolve an identification ridge. Specifications whose chain coordinates outnumber the latent path probabilities are refused as well.

Bootstrap resamples whose occasions or factor levels change the coefficient set are recorded as failed resamples. Intervals use retained resamples only, with a warning and recorded reasons, and are conditional on those resamples supporting the requested coefficients. With drop_empty = FALSE, both engines count every positive-weight row in the individual BIC; the default counts rows that observe an indicator. Initial or transition probabilities at the effective numerical bound also set boundary = TRUE in both engines; bootstrap likelihood-ratio tests refuse such inputs, as they already do for general transition fits.

See also

get_results() for the transition table and the assignments; plot_transitions() and plot_sequences(); multilpa() for the cross-sectional model whose measurement this one shares; enumerate_classes() to compare numbers of profiles.

Examples

# Model engagement transitions across each student's course sequence.
fit <- lta(
  course_engagement,
  vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance"),
  id = "student", n_profiles = 2, time = "sequence", n_starts = 2, seed = 1
)
get_results(fit, what = "transitions")
